Title: Chan Sow Lin scrapyard fire: No casualties, warehouse completely destroyed
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Smoke continued to rise from a scrapyard in Jalan Chan Sow Lin here this morning, hours after a fire completely destroyed the warehouse.
Pudu Fire and Rescue Station assistant superintendent Rahmat Kamaruzaman said the lingering smoke was caused by residual engine oil on half-cut car parts, which generated heat when water came into contact with the materials.
He said dismantling work using a JCB excavator would begin after the fire department's forensic team completed its investigation to allow the debris to be inspected and the fire fully extinguished.
"We expect firefighting operations to be completed by 1pm.
"The cause of the fire and estimated losses are still under investigation. No injuries or fatalities were reported," he told reporters at the scene today.
[[nid:1581824]]
Rahmat said the Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department operations centre received an emergency call at 5.53am, and the first fire engine arrived 10 minutes later.
"The fire was brought under control at 7.03am to prevent it from spreading to a nearby factory.
"Firefighters used offensive and defensive tactics from inside and outside the building to contain the blaze.
"Overhaul work was also carried out with assistance from Kuala Lumpur City Hall, which deployed a JCB excavator and shovel, as well as its rescue squad and the Malaysian Civil Defence Force," he said.
A total of
75 personnel, including seven senior officers
from seven nearby fire stations, were involved in the operation.

Title: Selangor on track to surpass RM100bil in investments this year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Selangor is on track to surpass RM100 billion in approved investments by year-end, Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said.
He said the state secured RM87.9 billion in approved investments in the first nine months of 2026, exceeding its RM80 billion annual target.
The investments involved 1,302 approved projects expected to generate 34,971 jobs.
Amirudin said Selangor continued to lead the country in the number of approved projects.
His remarks were delivered by state investment, trade and mobility executive councillor Ng Sze Han at the Selangor Investors Appreciation Awards 2025.
"Selangor is firmly on track to cross the historic RM100 billion threshold once again by the end of 2026," he said, noting that the state had achieved nearly 90 per cent of its original annual investment target by mid-year.
Invest Selangor Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Hasan Azhari Idris said the services sector accounted for the largest share of approved investments at RM74.5 billion.
He said the latest figures reflected Selangor's continued appeal as an investment destination following its performance in 2025, when it secured RM83.9 billion across 2,562 projects, exceeding its RM65 billion annual target.
Domestic investments accounted for RM48.9 billion of the 2025 total, while foreign investments contributed RM35 billion. The projects were expected to generate 61,311 jobs.
Amirudin attributed the state's investment momentum to continued confidence among global investors, particularly those from China, Singapore, Japan, the United States and Hong Kong.
"Global investors choose Selangor because we deliver certainty: world-class connectivity, an established ecosystem and seamless access to Asean and international markets," he said.
He said Selangor's economy expanded by 6.3 per cent, outpacing national growth despite global economic headwinds and geopolitical uncertainties.
Amirudin said Selangor aimed to become the first Malaysian state to surpass RM500 billion in economic value, with ambitions to expand its economy to RM600 billion in the near future.
Under the Second Selangor Plan 2026–2030, the state is targeting RM330 billion in cumulative investments, focusing on high-value sectors such as electrical and electronics, aerospace, automotive, the digital economy and the creative economy.
"Our focus is squarely on high-value frontiers, including expanding Phase 2 of the Malaysia IC Design Park to generate 800 advanced engineering roles.
"The Selangor Aeropark and Subang Airport Regeneration Plan would also anchor more than two-thirds of the nation's aerospace sector," Amirudin said.
He also highlighted the proposed Lembah Beringin High-Tech Auto Valley, aimed at driving electric mobility, and the Digital Future Action Plan 2030 to accelerate digital adoption.
Amirudin said infrastructure projects, including the East Coast Rail Link and proposed Selangor Rail Corridor, would strengthen connectivity between industrial centres, ports and regional markets.
He added that Speed Selangor would guarantee statutory development approvals within 30 days, providing greater certainty for investors.
Meanwhile, Hasan said Invest Selangor's role had expanded beyond investment promotion to facilitating projects and helping investors navigate regulatory requirements, site selection and reinvestment opportunities.
"Attracting investment is only the first step. At Invest Selangor, our core mission is providing assistance and ensuring a seamless business journey," he said.
Hasan said the agency was also strengthening ties between local small and medium enterprises and multinational corporations to improve access to technology, develop capabilities and help local businesses enter global supply chains.
Selangor was also positioning itself as a strategic gateway to Asean through international engagements and cross-border initiatives such as SIBS@ASEAN, he added.
"Our focus will go beyond attracting investment numbers.
"We want to attract quality investments that generate higher-value economic activities, create skilled employment opportunities, strengthen local industries and deliver meaningful benefits to the people of Selangor," Hasan said.
The Selangor Investors Appreciation Awards recognised investors in the manufacturing and services sectors for the highest new and expansion investments, as well as the most preferred investment locations by local authority and district.
In the manufacturing sector, Actmax International Holdings Sdn Bhd and Linergy Power Sdn Bhd received the highest new investment awards for local and foreign companies, respectively.
Baba Products (M) Sdn Bhd and NXP Malaysia Sdn Bhd won the highest expansion investment awards.
In the services sector, Bestari Solar Sdn Bhd and DHL Express (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd were recognised for the highest new investments, while SJP Medical Centre Sdn Bhd and KLN Logistic (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd received the highest expansion investment awards.
Majlis Bandaraya Diraja Klang was named the most preferred local authority for investment, followed by Majlis Perbandaran Hulu Selangor and Majlis Bandaraya Shah Alam.
Petaling was named the most preferred investment district, followed by Klang and Hulu Selangor.

Title: Houthis accuse Saudi forces of killing 19 in attack on civilian boat
Article:
SANAA: Houthi authorities accused on Friday Saudi forces of attacking a civilian boat and killing 19 people, after Yemen's dormant civil war reignited.
Conflict flared up in July after years of relative calm, pitting the internationally recognised government, backed by Saudi Arabia, against the Iran-backed Houthis.
Houthi health ministry spokesman Anees Alasbahi condemned on Friday the "horrific massacre committed by the Saudi enemy planes, which targeted a civilian boat carrying more than 25 displaced persons... which resulted in the martyrdom of 19 civilians and left 4 others wounded."
"Targeting civilians and displaced persons constitutes a full-fledged war crime and a flagrant violation of international humanitarian law and human rights," Alasbahi added.
Among the dead were eight children and six women, according to the Houthis' Almasirah television channel.
The boat was travelling from Ras al-Ara to Hays in the country's south, Alasbahi said on X.
Houthi media, including Ansarollah and news agency Saba, reported on Friday that Saudi planes had struck Yemen's capital Sanaa.
They also launched attacks on Taiz, in the country's southwest, according to Ansarollah.
The long-running civil war in Yemen, one of the world's poorest countries, fell dormant in 2022 after a ceasefire was implemented, but reignited in recent months.
The Houthis are now nearing Aden, the interim seat of the internationally recognised government, having made sweeping territorial gains since the war resumed.
More than 1,600 people have been killed in the latest round of fighting and more than 300,000 displaced, according to the United Nations.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Air Force One reporters' phones locked away over China spying fears
Article:
ABOARD AIR FORCE ONE: Reporters traveling with US President Donald Trump were asked to surrender cell phones they had used in China in a rare security precaution as Air Force One prepared to leave Shenzhen on Thursday.
"A staffer collected a number of cellphones from poolers when we got on the plane and placed them in a Faraday bag, designed to block signal," a White House pool reporter said in a note upon returning to the US.
"This was explained to us as being a necessary cybersecurity precaution against potential spying attempts," the report added.
According to the separate video pool report, a presidential aide collected temporary "burner" phones used by White House staff during the China visit for disposal or data wiping.
Journalists were asked to place devices they had used in the country into signal-blocking bags until the aircraft landed in the United States.
The so-called Faraday bags are designed to shield electronic devices from wireless communications, reducing the risk of surveillance or data collection.
Burner phones are temporary devices used in place of regular cell phones to protect them from potential security threats.
The video pool report said many reporters and photographers had left their regular work and personal phones, laptops and smart watches inside the protective bags before landing in China on Wednesday.
Those devices were not collected and could be used on the return flight, while journalists who had relied on their regular cell phones during the visit were left without them.
The phones were returned to the pool reporters upon Air Force One landing stateside.
The unusual precautions followed Trump's meetings with world leaders in Shenzhen, including Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.--AFP

Title: Military security procedures need urgent review after RMAF drug case
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government must review security procedures at all military facilities following the arrest of five Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) officers suspected of involvement in a drug trafficking syndicate.
Malaysian Institute of Integrity member Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye said the case raised serious questions about integrity, discipline and the effectiveness of internal security controls within the armed forces.
He described the alleged use of military aviation facilities to smuggle 96.64kg of suspected methamphetamine worth RM4.83 million as deeply disturbing, particularly as it involved personnel entrusted with national security.
"The alleged exploitation of military air transport facilities raises serious concerns about cargo screening, access control, supervision and monitoring. These safeguards must be strengthened immediately to prevent any recurrence," he said in a statement today.
Lee also stressed the need for a thorough, independent and transparent investigation to establish the syndicate's full extent, identify its masterminds, trace its financial resources and determine whether other security personnel were involved.
He said no one should be shielded because of rank or position.
He said the Defence Ministry and RMAF must also conduct an integrity and accountability review, including stronger internal monitoring, regular inspections and effective whistleblower protection.
"The government must adopt a zero-tolerance approach towards drug trafficking and corruption within all security agencies. Those found guilty must face the full force of the law," he said.
Lee said the actions of a few individuals should not undermine public confidence in the armed forces, as most military personnel served the nation with dedication and professionalism.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fama warns against selling imported mangoes as Perlis Harumanis
Article:
KANGAR: The Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (Fama) has warned traders against misleading consumers by selling imported Indonesian mangoes as Perlis Harumanis.
Perlis Harumanis is a premium mango variety prized for its fragrant aroma, sweet taste and soft, orange-yellow flesh. Its limited seasonal supply and strong demand make it a sought-after fruit.
Fama Perlis director Mohd Anzara Azizan said the practice was detected in October through live broadcasts on social media platforms, including TikTok.
He said Fama had received four formal complaints, three through social media and one from the Harumanis Perlis Association, over the misuse of the state's iconic product name.
"Following complaints about the online sales, Fama Perlis worked with the Market Regulation Division at Fama headquarters and in Selangor to raid a business premises in Bandar Baru Bangi, Selangor, on Nov 6.
"Inspections found that the company was marketing imported mangoes from Indonesia as 'Harumanis from Perlis' during a TikTok live broadcast, although the product boxes were clearly labelled as Indonesian avocado mangoes," he said at a press conference.
Anzara said the company's representatives failed to prove that the fruit was the Harumanis variety.
The company was instructed to remove posts referring to Harumanis and use the correct product name in line with its import documents and the 2008 Grading, Packaging and Labelling (GPL) Regulations.
He said Fama had carried out more than 120 premises inspections in Perlis this year, detecting inaccurate names such as 'Harumanis Surabaya'.
"Most traders have complied with our warnings and changed their labels. However, firm legal action will be taken if they repeat the offence," he said.
He said Perlis Harumanis, registered under the Geographical Indication, is mainly produced between February and June, while Indonesia's Arumanis mangoes (without the letter 'H') and avocado mangoes are produced between July and November.
"Some traders are taking advantage of the off-season by using the name Perlis Harumanis to boost sales.
"Fama does not prohibit legitimate imports, but traders must accurately state the product name, grade and country of origin, such as 'Indonesian Arumanis Mango' or 'Indonesian Avocado Mango', to protect consumers and local producers," he said.

Title: Pahang backs Tioman floating solar project, stresses need to protect marine environment
Article:
KUANTAN: The Pahang government is open to a proposed offshore floating solar research project at Pulau Tioman, provided it does not compromise the island's coastal environment.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the proposed site would be assessed to ensure the installation did not affect the coastal landscape, marine ecosystem, coral reefs, marine life or tourist safety.
He said the state supported the initiative as part of efforts to expand renewable energy use and transform Pulau Tioman into a green energy island.
"The study is being conducted to explore alternative electricity sources for Pulau Tioman, which currently relies on diesel-powered generation.
"However, long-term maintenance must also be given due consideration to ensure the project does not adversely affect the island's environment and tourism image," he said.
He was replying to Tioman assemblyman Datuk Seri Mohd Johari Hussain during the question-and-answer session at the state assembly sitting here today.
Johari had sought an update on the proposed project and the state government's position on its implementation.
​​​​​Wan Rosdy said the proposed 780kW offshore floating solar plant was a research project by Tenaga Nasional Bhd Research, in collaboration with SolarDuck and Hydro, to assess the technical and economic feasibility of offshore floating solar technology in Malaysia.
He said the proposal had been reviewed by the Technical Committee on Water and Energy Resources.
However, as the proposed site is within a marine park protected under the Fisheries Act 1985 and an area gazetted under the National Heritage Act 2005, the project must obtain the necessary approvals and comply with technical and legal requirements set by the relevant authorities.
Responding to a supplementary question from Johari on whether the project could replace diesel-powered electricity generation, Wan Rosdy said it was intended to reduce, rather than replace, the island's reliance on diesel.
"We only want to reduce our reliance on diesel, not replace it. We must comply with existing laws and do not want to harm the island, which is one of the world's most beautiful destinations.
"Environmental conservation and the protection of gazetted marine parks must be taken into consideration. We are ready to proceed based on the findings of the technical report," he said.

Title: Australian police arrest three after Sydney terror raids, one charged
Article:
SYDNEY: Australian police charged a man in Sydney with a terror-related offence and arrested two others after a series of early morning raids on Friday.
The man was alleged to have been using "ISIS inspired material" and researching how to build a car bomb for a potential attack, federal police told a press conference.
With the anniversary of the mass killing of 15 people at Bondi Beach approaching next month, deputy commissioner of national security for the federal police, Hilda Sirec, said Friday's arrest was likely to cause public fear but stressed the incident was not connected to the anniversary.
"We acknowledge we are just weeks away from the first anniversary of the Bondi Beach attack. There is no information to suggest that this alleged offending is connected to the anniversary of that attack," she said.
Search warrants had been executed across 10 Sydney suburbs by the New South Wales Joint Counter Terrorism Team.
A 35-year-old was charged with knowingly making a document "connected with terrorism" and possessing violent extremist material, a police statement said.
"The violent extremist material includes ISIS inspired material. It will be alleged in court the man was researching how to build a vehicle borne improvised explosive device which we allege was for potential use in a terrorist act," Sirec said.
The man was believed to be acting alone, and there was no indication he had identified targets or locations for an attack, she added.
"There is no ongoing threat to public safety at this time," she said.
A 34-year-old man was also arrested and is expected to be charged with hindering a police investigation, and a 33-year-old man was expected to be charged with firearm offences, a police statement added.
Two gunmen killed 15 people in a mass shooting at a Jewish Hanukkah celebration at the beach in December, carrying out Australia's deadliest mass shooting for 30 years.--AFP

Title: Two RMAF personnel remanded a week over drug trafficking using military planes
Article:
TAWAU: Two Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) personnel have been remanded for seven days from today to assist in investigations into a drug trafficking case involving the use of military airplanes.
The remand order against the two suspects, a 28-year-old corporal and a 48-year-old warrant officer 2, was issued by magistrate Don Stiwin Malanjum following a police application at the magistrate's court here this morning.
The suspects were arrested during a police operation early today before being brought to court for the remand order.

Title: Ismail meets Tuanku Muhriz this morning, three Undang Luak also present [WATCH]
Article:
SEREMBAN: Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim arrived at Istana Hinggap here at 10.17am today for an audience with Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir amid the state's administrative impasse.
Tuanku Muhriz arrived at the palace at 9.30am, followed by three Undang Luak: Rembau Undang Luak Datuk Sedia Raja Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid, Sungai Ujong Undang Luak Datuk Klana Petra Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari and Jelebu Undang Luak Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi.
Ismail, who is also the Juasseh assemblyman, is understood to have sought an audience to discuss the impasse.
Last Monday, Barisan Nasional announced that Ismail, 67, had resigned as Menteri Besar. He was sworn in on Aug 2.
The following day, the Negri Sembilan palace said his resignation would only take effect with Tuanku Muhriz's consent, in accordance with the Negri Sembilan State Constitution 1959.
Tuanku Muhriz was also reported to have granted Ismail an audience from 5pm to 6.30pm that day.

Title: Tech takes a beating as AI trade comes unstuck despite Anthropic surge
Article:
HONG KONG: Tech firms led losses across Asia once again Friday as Anthropic's sparkling debut failed to muster a recovery in sentiment towards the artificial intelligence (AI) trade, with nerves frayed by worries over crisis-hit Nvidia, profitability and regulation.
After its record-breaking initial public offering, Claude-creator Anthropic soared 17 per cent on its first day as ordinary investors sought to grab a piece of the new kid on the block.
But the rally did nothing to drag other, more established firms higher as the uncertainty that has hung over the tech sector in recent months sapped confidence, sending Wall Street deep into the red.
Magnificent Seven members who led a scorching surge over the past two years continued a retreat that has characterised trade since the summer, as investors fret over AI profitability, eye-watering spending, rising borrowing costs and geopolitics.
Microsoft, Apple, Amazon and Tesla were all well down, along with Nvidia -- which is battling to deal with the fallout from a spy scandal that has led to the resignation of pivotal leader Jensen Huang.
The losses continued on US futures markets, with Anthropic dropping more than four per cent.
Traders have also been spooked by the US Commerce Department's move to close a loophole allowing Chinese companies to access Nvidia's powerful AI chips remotely, adding to worries that a new Democratic-led Congress will impose further regulations.
The selling followed through to Asia, where Tokyo, Seoul and Taipei -- home to the region's leading AI-linked firms -- tumbled between four and six per cent.
Japan's Nikkei 225 was dragged by losses of more than 10 per cent in Kioxia, Advantest and tech investor SoftBank, TSMC shed 4.5 per cent and MediaTek tanked 9.4 per cent as Taiwan's main stock market was dragged five per cent lower.
SK hynix and Samsung were around six per cent down as South Korea's Kospi dived more than four per cent.
Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore and Manila also took a pummelling.
"With volatility elevated, equity futures breaking support and high-beta assets under pressure, traders will increasingly look for signs of capitulation, stabilisation or a catalyst capable of reversing sentiment," said Chris Weston at Pepperstone.
"The risk is that selling becomes self-reinforcing. As volatility rises, risk limits tighten, leveraged positions are reduced and systematic strategies can add to the pressure.
"Whether Anthropic's IPO proves to be a defining moment for the AI trade remains to be seen. For now, the immediate priority is watching how markets settle into the weekend and whether buyers can regain control next week."
Investors are keeping tabs on developments in the Nvidia case as California announced it was investigating whether the firm misled the public and investors about its chips ending up in China, despite federal export controls.
Huang resigned last week after reports alleged he had multiple extramarital affairs, including with a woman named Alice Huang who is a suspected Chinese spy.
Alice Huang, who is no relation, is the former director of Megaspeed, a cloud computing company based in Singapore that was investigated by local officials in 2025 over potential export control violations.
Jensen Huang has agreed to attend a closed-door questioning session about national security issues with Congressional officials on Dec 1.
Oil prices edged up after the International Energy Agency (IEA) said the crisis in the Middle East had created the "largest threat" to energy security in history.
The IEA said in its annual World Energy Outlook that consumers were increasingly footing the bill as the world runs out of ways to absorb the impact of the conflict on energy supplies.

Title: No more visa-free access to Malaysia for Indian citizens from Dec 31
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will end visa-free entry for Indian citizens on Dec 31.
In a written parliamentary reply to Datuk Seri Dr Ismail Abd Muttalib (Maran), the Home Ministry said the move was intended to strengthen pre-arrival screening and improve entry controls.
The visa exemption was initially introduced for one year, until Dec 31, 2024, before being extended for another two years to cover Indian and Chinese citizens.
It allowed eligible Indian visitors to enter Malaysia without a visa for stays of up to 30 days for tourism, business and social visits, subject to immigration requirements. Employment and study were not permitted.
The Immigration Department recorded 916,821 Indian visitors in the first year of the exemption, a 223 per cent increase from 2023.
The ministry said the government had adopted a three-pronged approach covering pre-arrival screening, checks upon arrival and enforcement against foreigners already in the country.
Other measures included ending the Multiple Entry Visa facility for short-term social visits by citizens of visa-exempt countries, including China, from Sept 1.
The restriction was intended to prevent repeated visits from being used for illegal employment or business activities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Citi underestimated risky assets by US$35 billion after incorrectly recording trades, sources say
Article:
NEW YORK/LONDON: Citigroup underestimated its risk-weighted assets (RWA) after an error in recording some trades, according to people familiar with the matter, forcing the US lender to inject capital into a subsidiary.
It is a setback for the US lender that is seeking to rapidly address years-long regulatory demands and represents another challenge for Citi chief executive officer Jane Fraser, who has been trying to fix various problems at the bank for years.
Citi has operated under tight supervisory scrutiny in the US, and as recently as the summer was targeting submitting paperwork to regulators this year to get the restrictions lifted, Reuters has reported.
The bank underestimated the risk-weighted assets by about US$35 billion at a trading unit in Europe, one person familiar with the matter said.
The bank recorded some trades incorrectly, which meant it underestimated its risk-weighted assets, two people said. The size of RWA is a key measure used by regulators to determine how much capital banks need to hold as a buffer for potential losses.
In a statement to Reuters, Citigroup said the bank had identified and resolved an internal capital modeling issue at a European trading subsidiary this summer. "The subsidiary remained fully compliant with regulatory minimums throughout, with no impact on the holding company or main operating bank," the bank said.
"Citi completed remedial actions and injected capital to immediately restore the subsidiary's buffers."
The Wall Street firm incorrectly recorded trades at its UK securities unit using an internal model based on its own statistical assumptions, the people said. Regulators had not approved the model for those types of transactions, they added. Once the trades were recorded using a standard risk model, the value of RWAs shot up significantly, the people said.
The third-largest US bank reported about US$1.2 trillion of total RWA in June and September, filings show, indicating the error represented about 2.7 per cent of the total. Reuters could not establish if the bank has already reflected the adjustment to RWA in the reported figures.
CITI'S PROBLEMS
Citi's problems stretch back to 2020, when it was told to remediate longstanding risk management and data governance problems identified by the US Federal Reserve and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.
The bank was fined US$400 million and agreed to a long list of longstanding issues it needed to fix, but was then fined another US$136 million in 2024 for the delay in fixing its data management problems.
The Federal Reserve had no comment on the underestimation of RWA when contacted by Reuters. The comptroller could not be immediately reached outside regular business hours.
Shaking off the regulatory shackles would free up resources, become a key achievement for Fraser and bolster Citigroup shares, according to analysts.
The bank has also been reprimanded for breaches in Europe. In 2024, UK regulators fined Citigroup the equivalent of US$78.5 million for controls failings in its trading operations, one of the biggest sanctions for systems breaches. In one of the blunders, Citi had caused a sudden fall in European stocks in May 2022.
Separately, Britain's Prudential Regulation Authority had fined the bank US$56.3 million in 2019 for providing inaccurate financial statements.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anthropic's Australian data centre overwhelmingly opposed by residents
Article:
SYDNEY: A data centre planned in regional Australia with Anthropic as its anchor tenant is overwhelmingly opposed by residents, a filing for the project showed, setting the scene for a showdown between the AI company and the community hosting its first Australian facility.
Of nearly 600 public submissions on the proposed Western Downs Digital Park, about 250 km (155 miles) west of Brisbane, two expressed support for the project and one was neutral, according to the filing. The remaining 595 opposed it or asked for a delay until developers cleared certain environmental hurdles, the filing said.
"A significant number of submissions raise reasonable matters regarding water, power, noise, roads, housing and the scale of the project," the filing, lodged on behalf of developer Zerra DC, said.
Representatives of Zerra and Anthropic were not immediately available for comment.
The initial response, though far from binding, gives a sense of the souring relationship between communities and the so-called AI factories being built at a pace around the world in a boom McKinsey has valued at US$7 trillion by 2030.
Already in Australia, Goodman Group scrapped a roughly A$1.2 billion data centre planned for Sydney in September after a public backlash, while NextDC delayed a project in Melbourne amid resident concerns about energy use, triggering a shares selldown.
The Anthropic project is on farmland and further from the suburbs, but with a planned computing load of 1.44 gigawatts, it would be one of the country's biggest. About one-third of the submissions were from people who lived within 200 km of the site, the filing said.
Objectors mostly cited concerns about water use, electricity demand and prices, noise, road damage from construction traffic and pressure on housing.
Before the data centre project named Anthropic as its tenant on September 15, it had received five objections in a month, a log of public comments showed, with the rest arriving between then and November 11, when the local government stopped accepting submissions.
The filing about Australian data centre submissions was published the same week Anthropic made its stock market debut on Wall St, pricing its initial public offering on November 18 in a deal that valued the company at around US$1.5 trillion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Emirates to add second A380 to KL, carries 12mil passengers in Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Emirates has carried nearly 12 million passengers to and from Malaysia over the past three decades as the Dubai-based airline prepares to increase seat capacity on its Kuala Lumpur route with a second daily Airbus A380 from Dec 1.
Emirates country manager in Malaysia Saeed Mubarak said the airline had expanded from three weekly flights when it entered the Malaysian market in October 1996 to 21 weekly services today, while increasing its cargo capacity and introducing newer aircraft and cabin products.
"Our growth in Malaysia over the past three decades is reflected in the expansion of our flight frequency, aircraft deployment and cargo capacity, alongside our continued investment in connectivity and the customer experience," he told Business Times in an interview recently.
Emirates' cumulative figures showed that the airline had operated 44,312 flights and transported some 335 million kilogrammes of cargo to and from Malaysia between Oct 1996 and Oct 2026.
The airline began operations in Malaysia on Oct 27, 1996, with three weekly flights from Dubai to Kuala Lumpur via Dhaka, using a Boeing 777-200.
It currently operates three daily nonstop flights between Kuala Lumpur and Dubai using an A380, an A350 and a retrofitted B777-300ER.
Saeed said the airline will replace its daily B777-300ER service with a second A380 from Dec 1 to accommodate passenger demand during the winter travel season.
The additional A380 will feature First Class, Business Class and Economy Class cabins, while the A350 will continue operating on the route.
The change will increase seat capacity without adding to Emirates' existing three daily frequencies.
Saeed said passenger demand between Malaysia and Dubai is supported by Malaysian outbound travellers, international visitors travelling to Malaysia and passengers connecting through Dubai to destinations across Emirates' global network.
Dubai remained a destination for Malaysian travellers visiting for leisure, shopping and business, while also providing connections to over 130 destinations worldwide, including cities in Europe, the Americas, Africa and the Middle East.
He said inbound tourism is another important market segment, with Emirates working with Tourism Malaysia to promote the country's attractions among travellers across its network.
On the airline's forward bookings, Saeed said Emirates has reported positive trends for the winter travel season across its global network with several markets tracking ahead of the previous year.
Between July and August 2026, Emirates carried more than 8.6 million passengers globally while maintaining healthy seat load factors.
Saeed said the airline continues to operate its three daily Kuala Lumpur-Dubai flights despite geopolitical tensions and airspace restrictions affecting aviation operations in the Middle East.
"While geopolitical tensions and airspace restrictions have created challenges for the aviation industry, Emirates has progressively restored its operations and is now operating at around 91–93 per cent of its pre-disruption capacity," he said.
He said passenger safety remained the airline's priority with operations adjusted when necessary according to developments in the region.
Emirates has also introduced more flexible booking arrangements for affected passengers, including date changes without change fees on eligible tickets and reduced refund fees on selected fares.
Passengers whose journeys were disrupted could also receive accommodation assistance and be rebooked to their final destinations, where applicable.
Saeed said competition among international airlines serving the Malaysian market had increased over the years, providing passengers with more choices of airlines, aircraft and connecting hubs.
He said Emirates continues to invest in its aircraft and onboard services to maintain its position in the market, including the introduction of its A350 and retrofitted B777 aircraft.
The airline introduced Premium Economy on its Kuala Lumpur services last year and has received a positive response from Malaysian passengers, particularly those travelling on longer journeys through Dubai to Europe and the Americas.
"Malaysian travellers are particularly value-conscious and consistently seek products and services that offer good value for money," Saeed said.
As of September 2026, Emirates has completed its retrofit programme on 107 aircraft globally, bringing its latest cabin products, including Premium Economy, to 143 aircraft.
The airline is also introducing further onboard improvements, including high-speed Starlink inflight connectivity and upgraded cabin features.
On airfares, Saeed said several factors influenced ticket prices, including jet fuel costs, seasonality and market conditions.
On the possibility of expanding Emirates' operations to other Malaysian cities, Saeed said the airline continues to evaluate network opportunities based on passenger demand, market potential and operational requirements.
"As with all our network decisions, any additional frequencies or new destinations are carefully evaluated before being introduced. We consider several factors with consumer demand and market potential being key considerations," he said.
Emirates currently extends its connectivity beyond Kuala Lumpur through its codeshare partnership with Batik Air Malaysia, which began in October 2023.
The agreement allows Emirates passengers to connect to five domestic destinations, namely Penang, Langkawi, Johor Bahru, Kota Kinabalu and Kuching, as well as three regional destinations — Singapore, Jakarta and Denpasar.
Meanwhile, Saeed said Emirates SkyCargo continues to support Malaysia's international trade through the belly-hold capacity of the airline's three daily widebody passenger flights.
Emirates currently provides close to 700 tonnes of cargo capacity weekly from Malaysia, serving businesses exporting goods to international markets through Dubai.
Malaysia's key outbound commodities include electronics and components, consumer products, aviation and oil and gas spare parts, and renewable energy equipment such as solar panels.
Across East and Southeast Asia, Emirates SkyCargo transported over 439,000 tonnes of cargo from 12 markets in its 2025/2026 financial year, representing about five per cent growth from the previous financial year.
On the possibility of introducing dedicated freighter services to Malaysia, Saeed said any expansion would require an assessment of cargo demand, market conditions and operational requirements.

Title: Missing screening stickers tip off RMAF personnel to drug smuggling bid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Five pieces of luggage without security screening stickers raised the alarm that led to the discovery of 96.6kg of drugs in an attempted smuggling operation at the Royal Malaysian Air Force's (RMAF) Subang Air Base on Tuesday.
RMAF chief General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris said personnel noticed the bags had not gone through the required screening process, prompting further checks.
"An Air Movement Section (AMS) personnel conducting a routine patrol discovered the luggage and a box near the arrival and baggage claim area.
"The five bags were wrapped in plastic and did not bear stickers indicating that they had undergone security screening.
"The accompanying box contained six bottles labelled as chemical fertiliser, which was also prohibited from being carried aboard an aircraft," he told the New Straits Times.
Norazlan said the luggage was subsequently taken to the scanning machine, where security personnel from the RMAF's Air and Ground Defence (Handau) unit detected suspicious packages neatly arranged inside.
"It was also established that the officer was part of the crew operating a logistics flight. He was summoned to open the bags for a physical inspection.
"When informed that the luggage had not passed security screening, the officer allegedly attempted to avoid taking the bags aboard the aircraft and instead returned them to his car," he said.
Norazlan said the Handau personnel refused to allow this and insisted that the bags be opened for inspection.
"As the officer did not have the keys, a Handau personnel assisted in opening the bags using a knife.
"The inspection uncovered torn red packages containing crystal-like substances suspected to be drugs.
"The discovery was immediately reported through the Handau chain of command before the Central Zone Criminal Investigation Branch was alerted," he said.
A subsequent inspection found that the substances were suspected to be crystal methamphetamine.
"We informed the federal police Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department team where they arrived at the scene at 5.20pm to conduct preliminary screening.
"The tests indicated that the substances were positive for methamphetamine, amphetamine and MDMA," he said.
Norazlan said police seized all five bags and the box containing the fertiliser bottles as evidence.
"Two officers were arrested at Subang Air Base, while a third officer was detained at the Labuan RMAF air base on the same day to assist investigations.
"Three other officers and nine other ranks personnel, comprising Handau personnel, provost unit personnel and aircrew, were also taken to a police station to assist investigations," he said.
Earlier, federal police Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police and the RMAF had crippled a drug trafficking syndicate that used military assets, with 11 individuals, including five RMAF officers, arrested in Subang and Labuan.
The arrests followed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's disclosure of alleged involvement by military personnel, including RMAF pilots and officers holding the ranks of lieutenant and captain.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ismail's resignation as Negri Sembilan MB to be known after royal audience
Article:
SEREMBAN: The status of Datuk Ismail Lasim's resignation as Negri Sembilan menteri besar will be known after his second audience with Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir today.
Ismail, who is also Juasseh assemblyman, submitted his resignation letter to the Ruler on Monday but continued performing his duties as usual.
Ismail declined to comment on whether his resignation had been accepted or whether he would serve as caretaker menteri besar until a successor was sworn in.
He said the matter would become known after today's audience at Istana Hinggap.
"All will be clear after I have met the Ruler," he said yesterday, after launching the Negri Sembilan Zakat Month organised by the Negri Sembilan Islamic Religious Council.
BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir had earlier confirmed receiving a copy of Ismail's resignation letter.
Negri Sembilan Royal Comptroller Datuk Azizi Mohamad Ali said the resignation would only take effect with the consent of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
Constitutional expert Professor Dr Nik Ahmad Kamal Nik Mahmood said the Negri Sembilan Constitution 1959 contained no specific provision requiring the menteri besar to obtain the Ruler's consent to resign.
He said the audience was more a matter of palace protocol and courtesy, allowing the menteri besar to formally inform the Ruler of his decision.
Meanwhile, Negri Sembilan Umno has backed Ismail staying on as menteri besar, provided outstanding issues are resolved promptly.
Tampin Umno division chief Datuk Mohd Isam Mohd Isa said the uncertainty surrounding Ismail's position needed to be resolved to ensure the smooth administration of the state government.
He said it was also necessary to allow the State Legislative Assembly to convene and table the 2027  budget before the end of the year.
Ismail was sworn in as the ninth Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar on Aug 2 after the Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional coalition won 25 of the 36 state seats in the state election.

Title: 75 firemen battle blaze at Chan Sow Lin car scrapyard
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A car scrapyard in Jalan Utusan, off Jalan Chan Sow Lin, was 90 per cent
destroyed in a fire
early today.
Pudu Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Senior Fire Officer I Abdul Manas Abdul Wahab said the Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department operations centre received an emergency call at 5.53am.
He said fire engines from the Pudu station and six supporting stations were dispatched to the scene.
"Upon arrival at 6.03am, firefighters found the warehouse engulfed in flames.
"The fire was brought under control at 7.03am," he said in a statement today.
Abdul Manas said firefighting operations were conducted from all four sides of the building using offensive and defensive tactics.
Containment measures were also taken to prevent the fire from spreading to nearby buildings.
A total of 75 firefighters were involved in the operation, which was still ongoing.
No casualties had been reported.
A check at the scene found that firefighters were continuing efforts to extinguish the blaze completely.
Further details, including the cause of the fire, are expected to be released after the operation ends.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'A trust we must honour': Surgeon's emotional tribute to organ donor
Article:
KOTA BARU: A surgeon involved in the bone donation procedure of the late Muhammad Aidil Ahmad Zupardi, 23, at the Universiti Sains Malaysia Specialist Hospital (HPUSM), has shared his emotional experience of carrying out the operation.
Dr Syahr Musafir said he struggled to contain his emotions as he reflected on the trust placed in him by the deceased and his family.
"From yesterday (the day before) until today (yesterday), I felt overwhelmed and tears kept welling up. Even in the operating theatre, my eyes could not stay dry.
"I had not eaten anything since morning, but even by noon, I did not feel hungry. I do not know where the strength came from.
"The deceased donated his bones. It is a trust for us to retrieve them carefully, return him to his family with dignity, and ensure the bones are properly preserved so they can eventually be used to treat other patients. All of this is a trust," he wrote in a Facebook post.
Dr Syahr, who was involved in coordinating the bone donation, said he repeatedly reminded himself that the procedure was a responsibility entrusted to him and that he had to give his best.
"Do the best you can because this is a trust from the deceased and his family, from our team members and, above all, from Allah.
"Tears may well up, but even through those tears, we must do our best," he said.
He said everyone had a role to play, including the deceased, who continued to make a difference as an organ donor even after his death.
"What a noble soul. Thank you. To his family, including his parents and siblings, who agreed to and consented to the donation, you are also wonderful people. Thank you all.
"His two kidneys, lungs, liver and corneas have already helped many people.
"The donated bones will also help dozens of people enjoy a better quality of life.
"I am humbled and deeply moved. May the deceased be granted a place in heaven," he said.
Aidil was involved in a road accident last Monday. He was later pronounced brain dead.
His family agreed to donate his organs, and the procedure was performed at HPUSM yesterday.
Hospital staff also paid their final respects through an
Honor Walk
, while the hospital building was illuminated in green as a tribute and symbol of the organ donation procedure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor told to brace for high tides, more rain next week
Article:
KUALA SELANGOR: Selangor must step up preparations for the high-tide phenomenon forecast from Nov 23 to 27, particularly as heavier and more frequent rain is expected until tomorrow.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said preparations in flood-prone areas must be urgently reviewed following forecasts by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
He said priority should be given to pumping water out of residential areas and monitoring river conditions and sea levels.
"Our priority now is to speed up water-pumping operations in residential areas and monitor river conditions and sea levels.
"More frequent rain is expected until Nov 21, while the high-tide phenomenon is forecast from Nov 23 to 27. I want preparations for both situations reviewed urgently to prevent conditions from worsening," he said.
He was speaking after visiting the temporary relief centre at Sekolah Kebangsaan Dato' Maharaja Lela here last night.
Amirudin also presented compassionate cash aid to 377 flood victims from the Ijok and Jeram state constituencies, identified as the worst-affected areas as of yesterday, particularly homes around Parit Mahang.
Commenting on the prolonged flooding in Parit Mahang, which has persisted for nearly two weeks, he said the river bund had been breached twice by irresponsible parties despite earlier repair works.
He said a police report had been lodged over the intrusion into the river reserve, and a suspect had been detained to assist investigations.
The bund is being repaired again, while additional water pumps have been deployed to speed up the draining of floodwaters.
Earlier, Amirudin visited 157 flood victims from 42 families at the SK Sungai Binjai relief centre in Meru, which was opened for the first time this year.
He said the centre had previously been opened at least two to four times annually.
He attributed the improvement to the Flood Mitigation Plan (RTB) project, which involved river widening works by the Drainage and Irrigation Department (DID).
"This shows how our RTB projects can reduce the impact of flooding, even though several areas are still affected by high tides.
"The overflow is coming from other areas, not Sungai Binjai, as the RTB project there has significantly reduced the impact of flooding compared with previous years," he said.

Title: HLIB keeps "Buy" on Malayan Cement, target price RM7
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Cement Bhd's operating margins in the coming quarters are expected to remain stable despite the rise in Indonesian coal prices.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) said that Malayan Cement's use of alternative fuels and waste heat recovery system is able to mitigate further margin squeeze.
The firm said the elevated Indonesian coal prices of US$85 per tonne have largely been reflected in Malayan Cement's results for the first quarter (Q1).
Bulk cement prices that saw a slight decline to RM400 per tonne in recent months also added further pressure to the company's margins.
"Nevertheless, we think the margin pressure is manageable, mitigated by Malayan Cement's usage of alternative fuels and waste heat recovery systems. Malayan Cement also benefits from competitive procurement costs for low-calorific coal, supported by economies of scale and stable supply from Indonesian state-owned suppliers.
"As such, we believe operating margins in the coming quarters should remain broadly stable," it said.
Malayan Cement's core earnings came in at RM223.7 million in Q1, in line with HLIB and consensus' expectations at 26 per cent of the financial year 2027 (FY27) forecast.
HLIB trimmed its earnings forecasts for the company by one per cent and three per cent for FY27 and FY28, respectively, and also introduced earnings of RM953 million for FY29.
HLIB kept a "Buy" call on the stock with a target price of RM7.

Title: Limit your children's screen time, Fahmi tells parents
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has urged parents and the community to help children build healthy digital habits by reducing screen time and encouraging real-world activities.
In a Facebook post marking World Children's Day today, he said children had the right to grow up in a safe and protected environment, including online.
"An increasingly digital world requires us to help them build healthy habits. Cut screen time and make more room for play, movement, learning and interacting with the real world.
"Our responsibility is not just to protect them today, but to ensure they grow up healthy, confident and ready to face the future," he said.
World Children's Day is observed every Nov 20 to raise awareness of issues affecting children worldwide.

Title: Sunway Construction set for earnings surge on record RM12.5bil order book
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Construction Group Bhd is poised to deliver stronger earnings in the financial year 2027 (FY27), supported by faster project recognition following record contract wins and a growing unbilled order book, says Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB).
The construction group has secured nearly RM10 billion in contracts year-to-date, lifting its unbilled order book to a record RM12.5 billion as of September 2026.
HLIB said the group's sizeable tender book of RM15.7 billion, including data centre (DC) projects with a combined capacity of more than 600 megawatts (MW), would provide strong visibility for further order book replenishment.
It expects earnings to accelerate in FY27 as contributions from the newly secured projects gain momentum heading into 2027.
The firm also expects the impact of new restrictions imposed by the US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) on access to advanced US artificial intelligence technology to be limited for local contractors.
While the restrictions could slow the development of data centres operated by Chinese-linked companies in Malaysia, HLIB said such projects typically engaged China-based contractors.
It noted that the group had predominantly secured data centre contracts from US hyperscalers, which were expected to remain insulated from the new restrictions.
On its financial performance, Sunway Construction recorded core earnings of RM104.7 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), up 25.4 per cent from RM83.5 million a year earlier and 1.4 per cent from the preceding quarter.
This brought its nine-month core profit after tax and minority interests (Patami) to RM323.1 million, an increase of 19 per cent year-on-year.
HLIB said the results were within its expectations, accounting for 78 per cent of its full-year forecast, and 73 per cent of consensus estimates.
The quarterly earnings were adjusted mainly for net foreign exchange losses of RM3 million and a reversal of receivables impairment losses amounting to RM3.4 million.
Sunway Construction also declared a third interim dividend of 7.9 sen per share, bringing its financial year-to-date dividend to 34.7 sen, compared with 41.5 sen in the corresponding period last year.
Following the results, HLIB has maintained its earnings forecasts and "Buy" recommendation on the stock, with an unchanged target price of RM10.
The target price is based on 23 times FY27 earnings per share, representing a premium of 0.5 standard deviation above its two-year average price-to-earnings ratio of 22 times.
HLIB said the premium valuation was justified by Sunway Construction's strong exposure to the data centre growth theme, execution capabilities and consistent margin delivery.
This is alongside higher returns on equity and an attractive dividend yield of six per cent, based on a 150 per cent payout ratio.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Petronas Gas poised to benefit from data centre-driven power demand
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Petronas Gas Bhd is poised to sustain its earnings trajectory, supported by the upcoming commercialisation of several key projects and rising demand for gas-powered electricity generation amid the rapid expansion of data centres.
In a note, Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) said the group is expected to benefit from the commercialisation of its Pengerang Cold Energy air separation unit in November 2026, followed by the Kimanis 2 and Sipitang power plants by the end of 2026.
Other projects include PG Lingkaran Fibre, expected to commence operations in the first quarter of financial year 2027 (Q1 FY27); the Labuan power plant in late 2027 to early 2028; and the Third Regasification Terminal (RGT3) Lumut project in 2029.
The firm noted that Petronas Gas was also evaluating plans for a new biomethane facility.
It added that the group stood to benefit from Malaysia's transition towards gas-powered electricity generation, which was accelerating to support the rapid expansion of data centres.
On its financial performance, HLIB said Petronas Gas' Q3 FY26 core net profit rose 7.6 per cent year-on-year to RM477.1 million, bringing its nine-month FY26 core net profit to RM1.37 billion, up 0.8 per cent.
For the nine-month period, stronger gas transportation and regasification contributions were offset by weaker gas processing and utilities performance, as well as higher net finance costs.
HLIB said the nine-month performance was within expectations, accounting for 74.2 per cent of the firm's full-year forecast and 75.1 per cent of consensus estimates.
The group also declared a second interim dividend of 18 sen per share, bringing its cumulative financial year-to-date interim dividend to 50 sen per share. The shares will go ex-dividend on Dec 9, 2026.
Overall, HLIB maintained its earnings forecasts and a "Hold" call on the group, with an unchanged sum-of-parts-derived target price of RM17.83.
HLIB said Petronas Gas' earnings were expected to remain stable as most of its business segments were protected under the regulated asset base framework, while its utilities segment was partly insulated by the imbalance cost pass-through mechanism.
It also expected the group to maintain its annual dividend payout of 72 sen per share, supported by a healthy annual free cash flow of between RM1.5 billion and RM2 billion.

Title: HLIB raises Sunway Healthcare earnings forecasts after strong results
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) Research raised its earnings forecasts for Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd by 8.8 per cent, 12.2 per cent and 12.5 per cent for financial years 2026 to 2028, respectively, following its recent stronger-than-expected results.
The revisions reflect higher revenue assumptions and a lower core effective tax rate, HLIB Research said in a note.
The research firm also raised its target price for Sunway Healthcare to RM2.20 from RM2.05, while maintaining its "Hold" call on the stock.
The revised target price is based on an unchanged 30 times financial year 2027 enterprise value-to-earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation valuation multiple.
HLIB Research said the implied upside to the revised target price remained below 10 per cent, insufficient to warrant a more constructive stance at current levels.
"Sunway Healthcare reported third-quarter financial year 2026 core profit after tax and minority interests (Patmi) of RM102.9 million, up 24.9 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ).
"The results came in above both our 75 per cent and consensus 78 per cent full-year estimates," it said.
HLIB Research said the stronger performance was driven by higher-than-expected revenue, underpinned by resilient domestic demand, alongside a more favourable core effective tax rate.
Revenue increased 9.6 per cent QoQ, supported by broad-based growth in patient activity across inpatient, outpatient and daycare services.
Inpatient revenue grew 12.1 per cent, outpatient revenue rose 4.3 per cent, while daycare revenue increased 6.7 per cent.
Foreign patient revenue also improved, rising 7.4 per cent to RM91.2 million from RM84.9 million previously, supported by seasonal tailwinds.
Core Patmi grew 24.9 per cent QoQ, reflecting favourable operating leverage at Sunway Medical Centre (SMC) Velocity and SMC Penang, alongside contributions from SMC Damansara and SMC Ipoh.
HLIB Research said SMC Ipoh's incremental contribution, following the commencement of operations in April 2025, further supported topline growth.
Looking ahead, HLIB Research expects stronger QoQ revenue in the fourth quarter, driven by growing contributions from SMC Damansara and SMC Ipoh as both facilities gain further traction.
It also expects Ebitda margins to expand further, supported by favourable operating leverage across hospitals and seasonal tailwinds.
The research firm added that the fourth quarter delivered stronger margins in the private hospital sector, reflecting a more favourable mix of elective surgeries.

Title: APEC ministers call for WTO reform, deeper regional trade integration
Article:
SHENZHEN: Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) ministers have called for meaningful reform of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) to improve its functions and ensure it remains relevant and responsive to members' interests amid evolving global trade challenges.
In their Joint Ministerial Statement issued following the 37th APEC Ministerial Meeting, ministers acknowledged that WTO-agreed rules remain key to facilitating global trade and encouraged members to work together to improve the multilateral trading system.
"The impasse at the 14th WTO Ministerial Conference again underscored that the WTO has challenges and needs meaningful reform to improve all its functions, and to be more relevant and responsive to the interests of its members," the statement said.
It said ministers reaffirmed their commitment to advancing economic integration in the Asia-Pacific in a market-driven manner, including through the free trade area of the Asia-Pacific (FTAAP) agenda, while welcoming new areas of cooperation on trade and labour and state-owned enterprises.
"We acknowledge the benefits of digitalisation to enhance and facilitate trade," the statement said, highlighting efforts to digitalise customs procedures, promote paperless trade and facilitate cross-border recognition of electronic trade-related documents to improve efficiency and strengthen supply chain resilience.
On regional connectivity, the statement said economies should continue strengthening physical, institutional and people-to-people links, while enhancing cooperation on quality infrastructure development and investment.
"We underscore the critical role that transportation plays in economic growth by facilitating the movement of goods and people," it said.
The ministers urged economies to accelerate the modernisation, upgrading and digital transformation of transport infrastructure to improve safety, efficiency, accessibility and resilience.
The statement said ministers welcomed APEC's roadmap for innovative, competitive and resilient services, which would guide the region's work over the next decade, while supporting efforts to reduce unnecessary barriers and facilitate digitally delivered services.
On innovation, it said economies should foster an enabling environment for digital and emerging technologies adoption to enhance productivity, efficiency, resilience and competitiveness across the Asia-Pacific region.
"We encourage economies to address potential risks such as data breaches, online scams and deliberate misuse of digital and emerging technologies for malicious purposes," the statement said, while stressing the importance of data protection, privacy and trust in digital transactions.
It also underscored the importance of structural reform for innovation-driven economic growth, supported by the Strengthened and Enhanced APEC Agenda for Structural Reform (SEAASR) 2026-2030. It also looked forward to the publication of the 2026 APEC Economic Policy Report on structural reform and AI-driven digital transformation.
On economic resilience, the statement said ministers emphasised the importance of credible and flexible fiscal, monetary and financial policy frameworks to manage shocks, maintain macroeconomic stability and address medium-term vulnerabilities.
"We encourage strengthened energy security through cooperation on supply chain resilience, secure cross-border infrastructure interconnection and risk assessment," it said.
On micro, small and medium enterprises, it said they remain an important foundation of regional economies, contributing to employment, innovation, trade and economic growth, while calling for efforts to ease regulatory and compliance burdens and expand access to digital solutions, financing and global value chains.
"We support integrating digital and technical skills to ensure workers are prepared for in-demand jobs," the statement said, emphasising reskilling, upskilling, lifelong learning and efforts to ensure workers could adapt to changing labour market demands.
The ministers reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening APEC as the region's premier economic cooperation forum, while welcoming Vietnam's preparations to host APEC 2027 and Mexico's hosting of APEC 2028.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AI surge could strain US capacity and overheat economy
Article:
WASHINGTON: The booming rollout of artificial intelligence technology could strain the US economy's capacity and further boost inflation that the Federal Reserve will have to counteract, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said on Thursday, as AI firm Anthropic set a new record for an initial public offering of stock.
"The AI boom is contributing to the potential of overheating in the economy. I find it hard to ... look at that any other way," Goolsbee said in a conference call with reporters. "When you're getting major business investment, almost unprecedented levels of business investment, there's a high danger that the economy's capacity cannot handle that kind of a pig through the python."
Goolsbee said he sees the multitrillion-dollar pipeline of data centre projects already adding to what he referred to as "borderline, disturbingly high inflation rates" that are well above the Fed's 2.0 per cent target and potentially heading higher.
He said he felt the Anthropic IPO, giving the company's early shareholders the ability to tap equity holdings well in excess of US$1 trillion, could on its own become relevant to the path of the broader economy.
"A US$1.5 trillion IPO. The question of what people are going to do with the money now that they have some access to that liquidity is going to become a macro-relevant statistic," Goolsbee said. "We're watching that."
DATA-CENTER BACKLASH
The US central bank is widely expected to raise interest rates by a quarter of a percentage point at its December 8-9 meeting. Fed policymakers also are wrestling with how the AI boom is influencing the economy.
The recent US midterm elections saw AI scepticism emerge at the polls, with municipalities in a number of states approving ballot initiatives that could limit how quickly and where data centers get built, potentially slowing the industry's breakneck evolution.
At the same time, the Fed this week held a high-level conference looking at the possible impact on productivity and the labour market should the new technologies diffuse through the economy and reach a potential that Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has characterised as pivotal to US economic leadership.
In remarks at an earlier event on Thursday, Goolsbee said it was not yet clear what effect AI will have on productivity or the economy's underlying potential, noting that it took years — even decades — for other general-purpose technologies to change how businesses operated on a broad basis.
In the meantime, the Fed will have to cope with short-term effects that so far seem to be inflationary.
"The Fed's job is to prevent this thing from overheating the economy," with monetary policy set tight enough to keep demand and supply in balance, Goolsbee said at the event.
The Chicago Fed chief did not say if he would support a larger half-percentage-point rate hike at the December meeting, as at least one of his colleagues has advocated, but added that all options were on the table.
"The question of how steep the rate path is going to be and if there will be any rate increases should be determined, in my view, by whether you think inflation is going to be heading back to 2.0 per cent on its own or not," Goolsbee said. "The evidence does not suggest we're on a path back to 2.0 per cent."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US approved nearly 900,000 AI chip shipments to China in six months
Article:
WASHINGTON: The Trump administration approved shipments of nearly 900,000 advanced AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD for Chinese companies from December 2025 through May 2026, the House Foreign Affairs Committee said on Thursday.
The approvals for 879,000 chip shipments by the Commerce Department included 75,000 for Alibaba, 150,000 for Tencent, 43,000 for Baidu, and 4,000 for BYD, all on the Pentagon's list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies, the committee noted.
The unusual release of chip export licensing data comes as the administration of President Donald Trump faces heightened scrutiny following news about former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has fueled renewed calls in Washington for a tougher stance on China.
Companies had sought permission to ship over 3.4 million chips to China during the period, the documents showed. It was not immediately clear how many of the approvals resulted in actual China-bound shipments of chips, which included Nvidia's H200 and AMD's equivalent MI325X.
News surrounding Huang has turned a spotlight on instances of Nvidia AI chips being smuggled to China that went unpunished, dialling up pressure on the Trump administration to crack down on Chinese tech ​threats.
The Commerce Department said its approach to H200 licensing "is based on a rule published in the Federal Register in January 2026, which imposes significant additional national security-related requirements on license applicants in order to qualify for case-by-case consideration rather than a presumption of denial."
Chris McGuire, a former US official and expert on the US-China technology battle, said, "The fact that over 30 per cent of the AI chips sent to China were shipped to companies that the Department of War has designated as Chinese military companies is astonishing, and calls into question whether Commerce conducted any serious national security review before approving these licenses."
Nvidia said in a statement that the approvals were "subject to strict conditions and limited volumes." It added that "despite receiving some licenses, we have since stopped shipping H200s to China."
AMD said it "complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations."
Alibaba, Tencent, Baidu, BYD, the Commerce Department and the Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
MOST DETAILED PUBLIC DISCLOSURE
Former President Joe Biden had restricted Chinese access to the prized chips over fears that they would supercharge China's military and erode the US lead in artificial intelligence.
But Trump in December gave the green light for Nvidia to ship its H200 chip to China, rolling back Biden-era restrictions and drawing fierce criticism from China hawks across the US political spectrum.
Despite the approvals, questions swirled as to whether the AI chips were actually reaching Chinese shores.
In May, Reuters reported the US had cleared about 10 companies to buy the H200, but that no deliveries had taken place.
In testimony before the committee in July, Commerce Department official Jeffrey Kessler said shipments had begun but there had been 'very few.' Several major Chinese internet companies had each obtained about 10,000 H200 chips, Reuters has since reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
"This is the most detailed public disclosure in the history of the Export Control Reform Act," committee Chair Brian Mast, a Republican from Florida, said upon releasing the data, referring to 2018 legislation that expanded Commerce's authority to restrict the export of sensitive technologies for national security reasons.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Two family members killed in Parit Raja house fire
Article:
BATU PAHAT: Two family members were found burnt to death in a house fire in Kampung Parit Raja here early today.
The fire is believed to have started at 2.40am, but the identities of the victims have yet to be established.
Ayer Hitam Fire and Rescue Station senior operations commander Mohamad Shamim Mohamed Salikin said the department received an emergency call at 2.50am and dispatched 16 firefighters to the scene.
He said firefighters found a fire involving a semi-permanent house measuring 40 by 70 feet (about 12 by 21 metres).
"Firefighting operations were carried out using water from the fire engines' tanks from the Ayer Hitam and Penggaram fire stations.
"The fire destroyed 70 per cent of the house structure. Two victims were found burnt to death in the main bedroom.
"They are believed to be a mother and child, but their genders and ages have yet to be determined," he said in a statement.
Shamim said the operation was completed after firefighters ensured the scene was safe before handing it over to the fire department's forensic team for further action.
The cause of the fire and estimated losses are still under investigation.
